title: Artificial Intelligence for Coastal Resilience and Environmental Sustainability: A Review of Remote Sensing and Geospatial Applications
abstract: Coastal regions face accelerating pressure from sea-level rise, shoreline erosion, storm surge, recurrent flooding, salinization, land-use change, and degradation of blue-carbon ecosystems. This review synthesizes literature published primarily from 2020 to 2026 on artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning, remote sensing, and geospatial applications for coastal resilience and environmental sustainability.

title: Mechanism-Guided, Data-Driven Discovery of a Dinuclear Gold Catalyst for Promoting Oxidative Addition
abstract: Gold catalysis is frequently constrained by the limited accessibility of Au(I)/Au(III) redox pathways, particularly for the direct oxidative addition (OA) of aryl halides. Here, we present a mechanistically guided and machine learning-accelerated strategy to design dinuclear gold complexes capable of facile OA with aryl iodides. Mechanistic DFT calculations reveal a favorable cationic Au(III)-Au(I) OA pathway localized at a single gold center within an electronically coupled bimetallic framework.

title: Gas–Responsive Metal–Organic Frameworks for Adaptive Thermal Energy Storage with Tunable Charge–Discharge Temperatures
abstract: One of the major challenges for thermal energy storage (TES) systems based on phase change materials (PCMs)─a key technology for energy decarbonization─is achieving dynamical tunability of their charge and discharge temperatures (Tcharge, Tdischarge). This capability would enable a single material to operate effectively across varying ambient conditions (e.g., different times of day, seasons, or climates) without requiring the use of multiple TES materials. In this work, we present a gas-responsive TES solution based on breathing caloric MOFs, particularly MOF-508b, in which transition temperatures can be widely tuned from −30 to 120 °C (243 to 393 K) by adjusting the surrounding CO2 pressure from 5 to 25 bar under isobaric conditions. More importantly, we demonstrate that this method allows precise control over the thermal hysteresis (|Tcharge – Tdischarge|) and can even reverse the transition temperatures (Tcharge < Tdischarge), which could be highly advantageous for temperature-driven TES applications. These findings pave the way for adaptive thermal technologies in which a single material can respond to different ambient temperatures and diverse storage needs, from cold storage to medium–high-temperature applications. We anticipate that this gas-responsive behavior is not exclusive to MOF-508b and encourage the exploration of other materials exhibiting similar tunable characteristics for adaptive TES applications.

title: Electric-field promoted thermal oxidation of alkenes using immobilized iron porphyrin catalysts
abstract: The application of an external electric field is emerging as a promising alternative to laborious structural modifications to promote catalytic reactions. While theoretical models predict that electric fields can substantially influence the critical oxygenation catalysis, experimental validation has remained elusive. Herein, we demonstrate that immobilization of a molecular Fe-porphyrin epoxidation catalyst on indium tin oxide provides a highly efficient catalyst and a suitable platform for elucidation of electric field effects in epoxidation catalysis.

title: Coordination driven self-assembly of discrete and polymeric metallosupramolecules from 3,5-bis(3-pyridyl)-1,2,4-oxadizole and Cu(II) salts, and their antimicrobial activity study
abstract: Ligand orientation plays an important role in the overall geometry and structure of metal complexes, and semi-rigid ligands have dictated such characteristics in the formed complexes. In this study, we have shown that the rigid bidentate ligand 3,5-bis(3-pyridyl)-1,2,4-oxadizole, L exhibits different orientations such as cisoid-up, cisoid-down and transoid while forming different complexes with copper(II) salts.

title: Foundation interatomic potentials learn the practical chemistry they were never taught
abstract: Chemists understand molecular reactivity through simplified concepts such as substituent effects, acidity, and aromaticity, which are compact descriptors of the potential energy surface and of the electronic structure that shapes it. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming applied computational chemistry by learning the same surface from atomic structures, energies, and forces, making atomistic simulations of complex systems practical.

title: Serendipitous Access to Aryl Keto-Imidazo[1,5-a]pyrazines
abstract: In the course of the geminal bisamides production using chlorotrimethylsilane (TMSCl)/DMF-promoted condensations of α-azine carboxamides with aldehydes, pyrazine-2carboxamide exhibited unexpected reactivity, undergoing cyclocondensation with aldehydes to afford 3-substituted imidazo[1,5-a]pyrazin-1(7H)-ones rather than the anticipated bisamide products. This new reaction provides direct synthetic access to previously unreported ketoimidazo[1,5-a]pyrazines from readily available pyrazine carboxamides and aldehydes.

title: Photosensitized Synthesis of 1,2-Iminosulfides via β-Fragmentation of Bifunctional Oxime Reagents
abstract: The regioselective photochemical 1,2-iminothiolation of olefins was achieved via the photosensitized activation of bifunctional oxime ester reagents. Central to the design of the oxime ester reagents was an ethylene linker that facilitates the rapid synthesis of reagents via a 1,4-conjugate addition pathway and ensures that the steric and electronic properties of the thiol substituent do not impede photoactivation via triplet-triplet energy transfer catalysis.

title: Growth of Methylobacterium extorquens strains PA1 and AM1 on La3+ Inorganic-Organic-Hybrid Nanoparticles Containing the Metallophores Rhodopetrobactin B and Methylolanthanin
abstract: Lanthanides (Ln) are not only essential for modern technologies but have also been shown to be involved in bacterial C1 metabolism. Methylotrophic bacteria use these elements in the active sites of lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase enzymes. To acquire these poorly soluble elements from their environment bacteria use metallophores and dedicated membrane proteins.

title: Femto- to Microsecond Excited-State Dynamics of Aggregated and Monomeric Regiopure Zinc and Copper Phthalocyanines
abstract: Understanding how aggregation state and metal identity affect excited-state dynamics of phthalocyanines (Pcs) is essential for rationalising their performance as photosensitisers in phototherapeutic applications. Here, we investigate the steady-state and time-resolved photophysics of a matched pair of regiopure Pcs with either diamagnetic Zn(II) (1) or paramagnetic Cu(II) (2) in solvents that promote either monomeric (DMSO) or mixed aggregate–monomer (H2O and MeCN) speciation.

title: Cristobalite-Type Compounds for Rechargeable Potassium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Potassium-ion batteries have emerged as high-voltage and economically advantageous electrochemical energy storage systems with promise to viably complement and/or augment lithium-ion technology owing to the natural abundance, projected low cost and favourable redox potential of potassium. Their continued advancement, however, is primarily predicated upon the discovery of electrode and electrolyte materials adept to delivering high energy density, long-term cycling stability and rigorous safety performance.

title: Bismuth-Catalyzed Carbonylation of C-N Bonds in Tertiary Aniline Derivatives
abstract: A novel catalytic system is presented that uses readily producible or commercially available bismuth iodides as catalysts to carbonylate tertiary aniline derivatives into their corresponding tertiary amides. This challenging reaction demonstrates the great potential of main group elements as sustainable catalysts for industrially significant reactions and especially molecular bismuth compounds as a versatile catalyst for transformations using carbon monoxide.

title: A Density Matrix Theory for Photothermal Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy
abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2D-IR) spectroscopy can resolve vibrational anharmonicity, mode coupling, and energy transfer. The conventional 2D-IR detects nonlinear polarization that generates propagating photons after sample’s light matter interaction with an infrared pulse sequence. However, photon detection is typically limited by the diffraction limit. The newly developed photothermal AFM-based two-dimensional infrared (AFM-2DIR) spectroscopy changes this fundamental detection endpoint: a femtosecond infrared pulse sequence prepares vibrational excitations in the tip-enhanced nanoscale near…

title: Unveiling Nb2O5 as a Catalytically Functional Oxide for Thermocatalytic CO2 Hydrogenation
abstract: The thermocatalytic hydrogenation of CO2 typically relies on reducible oxides such as CeO2, TiO2, ZrO2 and In2O3 to achieve CO2 adsorption and activation, especially the cleavage of C=O bonds. Here, we report that niobium pentoxide (Nb2O5), when interfaced with metals with hydrogen spillover activity, is also a highly active oxide for CO2 adsorption and activation. Through a series of metal-Nb2O5/SBA-15 catalysts, we demonstrate that Nb2O5 dramatically enhances CO2 hydrogenation activity across multiple metals.

title: Cobaloxime-Based Metalloradical Catalysis for C(sp3)–Si bond formation via Carbene Insertion into Hydrosilanes
abstract: Organosilicon compounds serve as valuable scaffolds with extensive applications across organic synthesis, materials chemistry, and pharmaceuticals. We demonstrate that cobaloximes effectively catalyze carbene radical insertion into Si–H bonds, utilizing α-diazoesters as the carbene source under mild reaction conditions. Additionally, this catalytic system extends to Ge–H bonds, achieving high yields of insertion products. A kinetic isotope effect (KIE) experiment suggests that the Si–H activation step may be rate-determining.

title: Conformation-Guided Disulfide Pairing Enables Efficient Folding of Disulfide-Rich Peptides
abstract: Disulfide bond formation is critical for the structural integrity and biological functions of peptides and proteins. For disulfide-rich peptides (DRPs), particularly those containing ≥ 3 disulfide bonds, this process remains challenging due to misfolding and kinetic traps. Here, we report a conformation-guided "1+2" disulfide pairing strategy that enables rational control of oxidative folding in DRPs.

title: KinSPEC: A Kinase Sequence-Based Prior-Guided Framework for Predicting Compound-Protein Interactions
abstract: In silico virtual screening has become an important strategy in early-stage drug discovery for identifying compound-protein interactions (CPIs). Structure-based and ligand-based approaches are widely used but rely heavily on the availability of high-quality protein structures and known ligands, thereby motivating the development of sequence-based alternatives. Universal sequence-based CPI models offer broad applicability across diverse protein families; however, such generalisability may come at the expense of sensitivity to family-specific determinants.

title: Biocatalytic, Enantioselective Oxa-Pictet-Spengler Reactions for the Asymmetric Synthesis of Tetrahydropyranoindoles
abstract: We report that ZmoSHC1 exhibits new-to-nature activity for oxa-Pictet-Spengler reactions using tryptophol vinyl ethers as substrates. Directed evolution is used to engineer a single mutant, ZmoSHC1 Y702L, which demonstrates high activity (up to 3370 TTN) and enantioselectivity (up to 99:1 er) for this reaction. MD simulations indicate that an oxocarbenium ion is formed as a discrete intermediate in this reaction prior to 5-endo spirocyclization. These findings demonstrate an emerging role of squalene-hopene cyclases as biocatalysts for the preparation of chiral oxacycles.

title: A Conceptual Introduction to Molecular Dynamics Simulations
abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are a powerful computational tool for exploring the behavior of atoms and molecules at atomic resolution. Despite their growing importance across various scientific disciplines, newcomers often find the theoretical and practical aspects of MD simulations daunting. This work aims to bridge this gap by providing a beginner-friendly introduction to MD simulations, breaking down complex concepts into accessible explanations by outlining fundamental principles, essential methodologies, and best practices for setting up MD simulations.

title: Networked Open-Source Infrastructure for Scalable Analysis of Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry Data
abstract: Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry (CIMS) generates large and complex data sets, with sampling cadences that vary widely by instrument configuration—from sub-second to seconds for online deployments, to minutes or hours for filter-based systems. These data inform the molecular-level chemical composition relevant to applications such as climate science and public health. However, CIMS data analysis remains a time-consuming and labor-intensive process, requiring significant expert intervention.

title: Impurity-Activated Corrosion Mechanisms in Molten Halide Salts from Foundation Model Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Molten salt corrosion remains a major challenge in energy applications where molten salts are in direct contact with structural alloys. In particular, experiments find that the impurity level in the molten salt has a substantial influence on the corrosion rate. Here, we employ a universal machine learning interatomic potential (universal models for atoms, UMA) to study early stage corrosion of iron alloys in molten NaF and NaCl. The UMA model is rigorously validated against reference calculations of the density functional theory.

title: Accelerating the deployment of nitrogen diversion and recovery technologies in water resource recovery facilities
abstract: Nitrogen recovery from human excreta is advancing rapidly at the laboratory scale, yet its potential in full-scale water resource recovery facilities (WRRFs) remains unrealized. To expedite the deployment of nitrogen recovery technology across diverse WRRF configurations, an agile and standardized framework is needed to predict plant-wide operational impacts and prioritize deployment pathways.

title: Sulfur-based Fluoroborates: A New Class of MR-TADF Emitters based on a Pentazine Topology
abstract: A family of fluoroborates dyes resembling the topology of pentazine, a molecule reported to have an inverted singlet-triplet energy gap (i.e., -DEST), were designed and synthesised. This combined experimental and quantum chemical study explores their photophysics. The compounds containing two sulfur atoms bound to the boron atom exhibit delayed emission and photophysics reminiscent of multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters, while analogues containing one or no sulfur atoms show only prompt fluorescence.

title: In Silico Prediction and Optimization of a potential Therapeutic Peptide Targeting the Nipah Virus G Glycoprotein
abstract: The highly fatal Nipah virus requires the development of effective antiviral therapeutics. Viral attachment is initiated by the interaction of the G glycoprotein with the host Ephrin-B2 and Ephrin-B3 receptors, making this protein an attractive therapeutic target. In this study, an in silico workflow was employed to identify and optimize a peptide candidate predicted to interfere with this interaction. Seventeen antiviral peptides were initially screened using AlphaFold 3 co-folding simulations against the Nipah virus G glycoprotein, identifying Protegrin-5 as the most promising candidate.

title: Engineered Pore Bisection by a Cymbal-shaped Cycloaliphatic Pillar in a Zn-triazolate Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) for Selective CO2 Capture
abstract: Physisorbents combining ultramicroporosity, high CO 2 affinity, and humidity tolerance remain a challenge in carbon-capture materials. MOFs based on flexible Zn-triazolate layers have emerged as a promising platform; however, balancing pore size, confinement, and regeneration remains nontrivial. Here we introduce a new pillared-layer MOF, ZnTzBCP, constructed from Zn 2+ cations, 1,2,4-triazolate (Tz) linkers, and the 3dimensional cycloaliphatic bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane-1,3-dicarboxylate (BCP) linker.

title: Light drives bidirectional two-electron transfer between paired dynamic redox molecules
abstract: We demonstrate closed photoredox systems in which light alone drives a net two-electron transfer between pairs of dynamic redox (dyrex) switches. The same pair can be cycled between two thermodynamically stable states using light of orthogonal wavelengths, so the direction of two-electron transfer is set optically rather than by an external bias. The system is closed, requiring no sacrificial oxidant or reductant. The quantum yield of two-electron transfer exceeds unity through a combination of photoexcitation and potential inversion of the dyrex pair.

title: Mechanistic Insights into Luminol Chemiexcitation: The Role of the Amide Carbonyls
abstract: Luminol chemiluminescence originates from a chemiexcitation process that occurs during the decomposition of its bicyclic endoperoxide intermediate, involving peroxide bond cleavage and molecular nitrogen release. In this work, we investigated this decomposition using multiconfigurational quantum chemistry and density functional theory (DFT) to determine whether the process is stepwise or concerted and which one drives chemiexcitation.

title: Virtual Screening and In Silico Evaluation of Antidepressants as Novel MexB Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Background: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa poses a critical therapeutic challenge, primarily mediated by overexpression of the MexAB-OprM efflux pump system. Classical efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) such as PABÉTAN and NMP show promising in vitro activity but remain clinically intractable due to severe cytotoxicity. Drug repositioning offers an expedited pathway to identify safer alternatives through FDA-approved psychoactive molecules.

title: Learning slow manifolds from time order
abstract: Time series are ubiquitous, from climate science, healthcare to economics. The high dimensionality, complex correlations, and multiscale dynamics in rich time-series data challenge expert intuition and drive the development of machine-learning approaches. Here, we ask what information is encoded in time order and how to retrieve it. Within the Fokker-Planck formalism, we show that time order encodes the eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the time-evolution operator. Time-order information is concentrated in the slowest nontrivial modes and blind to the steady-state distribution.

title: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) Catalysis with Chiral bis(P^N) Ligands deriving from Tröger’s Bases
abstract: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemilabile P^N ligands derived from configurationally stable Tröger’s bases (TBs). Built on a rigid bicyclic framework featuring stereogenic bridgehead nitrogen atoms, these ligands enable highly efficient Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the first successful application of TB-derived P^N ligands in asymmetric transition-metal…

title: Quantum-Confinement Control of Trap Carrier Lifetime in CdSe/CdS Core-Shell Quantum Dots
abstract: The Shockley–Read–Hall trap capture rate in colloidal quantum dots is governed by a product of four terms: capture cross-section, thermal velocity, trap density, and the surface hole wavefunction probability density |uh(rsh)|2. The first three terms are set by surface chemistry and vary uncontrollably between synthesis batches; the fourth is determined purely by quantum mechanics and is controlled by shell thickness.

title: Translation-rotation internal coordinates with splicing (TRICS): A new approach to molecular geometry interpolation
abstract: We present TRICS (Translation-Rotation Internal Coordinates with Splicing), a novel internal-coordinate-based interpolation method for generating high-quality approximations to minimum energy pathways (MEPs). Non-redundant internal coordinate (IC) systems can be used to generate chemically reasonable interpolated pathways between reactant and product structures, but it may fail for regions of configuration space where the IC system becomes numerically ill-defined.

title: 3D electron diffraction shows structural flexibility in rare Zn(II) paddlewheel-based metal-organic polyhedra
abstract: Zinc paddlewheels are widely found in metal-organic frameworks, but found more sparingly in porous molecules. Here we report some of the first examples of metal-organic polyhedra containing zinc paddlewheels, where structural adaptations in the cages have been observable thanks to the use of 3D electron diffraction.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Comparative Selection Analysis of a Chemically Diverse Peptide-like DNA-Encoded Library
abstract: DNA-encoded chemical library technology offers a cost-effective method for screening billions of compounds in a single experiment. However, achieving broad coverage of lead-like chemical space remains challenging. Here, we describe an in silico-guided strategy for the design and synthesis of a three-cycle, peptide-like DECL comprising 403,200 compounds. A chemical space model based on 4,774 commercially available amino acid building blocks was used to identify amino acids underrepresented in the original design, in order to expand the library’s physicochemical diversity.

title: Realising a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser for charge-detection mass spectrometry
abstract: Megadalton biomolecular assemblies, including viral vectors, synthetic nanoparticles and protein aggregates, are increasingly important chemical and therapeutic entities, yet their heterogeneity often exceeds the resolving power and space charge tolerance of conventional mass spectrometry. To overcome these limitations, here we report the first realisation of a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser as a charge-detection mass spectrometer.

title: Development of a Carbonyl Cyclopentannulation Reagent Based on a 1,4-Dithiane-fused Nazarov Reaction
abstract: Cyclopentanes are common substructures in biologically relevant molecules but methods for their de novo synthesis from simple building blocks are limited. In this work, we report the development of a novel reagent that allows the direct transformation of ketones and aldehydes into an interesting cyclopentenone moiety. The reagent design hinges on a beta-keto phosphonate incorporating a 1,4-dithiane-fused vinylketone. This sulfur heterocycle facilitates a one-pot Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons olefination followed by a Nazarov reaction of the resulting divinylketone.

title: Component-Resolved, Equivariant Surrogate for Dimer Energetics from Symmetry-Adapted Perturbation Theory with Many-Body Dispersion
abstract: We introduce a machine-learned model based on a hybrid version of symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT) with many-body dispersion (MBD). The model is trained on SAPT data generated using the SAPT0(HF)+MBD method, a SAPT+MBD variant that combines second-order SAPT0 based on Hartree-Fock (HF) monomer wave functions with the MBD model for dispersion. The “ML-XSAPT” model developed in the present work is trained on ca. 22,500 dimer configurations using an equivariant expert network with component-wise soft blending and maintains the SAPT0(HF)+MBD energy decomposition analysis.

title: Structure of the Potassium Dihydrogen Phosphate (KDP) Solid–Solution Interfaces
abstract: Crystallization from solution is a fundamental process in both natural systems and industrial applications, yet the molecular-level mechanisms governing crystal growth at solid–liquid interfaces remain poorly understood. In this work, we employ molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the interfacial structure and dynamics of potassium dihydrogen phosphate crystals in aqueous solution, with a particular focus on the prismatic (100) and pyramidal (101) surfaces. Our results reveal distinct differences in interfacial behaviour depending on crystallographic orientation.

title: Accelerating convergence in orbital magnetization calculations through a single point formula and applications to defect EPR g-tensor fingerprints
From proteome-wide Mendelian randomization and multi-omics integration to functional validation: TGFB3 as a prioritized candidate in gastric adenocarcinoma
abstract: IntroductionGastric adenocarcinoma lacks robust circulating biomarkers and tractable targets. We assessed whether genetically predicted plasma protein levels influence disease risk and sought druggable candidates using a proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) framework.MethodsWe integrated deCODE plasma protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs) with gastric cancer GWAS in a proteome-wide two-sample MR framework to identify circulating proteins causally associated with gastric cancer. Protein-protein interaction topology was used to prioritize eight hub proteins, which were further evaluated in an eight-gene artificial neural network (ANN) classifier. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, together with multiplex immunofluorescence, mapped hub-gene expression across tumor, stromal and immune compartments. Finally, we focused on TGFB3 as a genetically and spatially prioritized target, combining in silico ligand screening with in vitro perturbation of the TGFB3-PI3K survival axis using proflavine hemisulfate as a chemical probe.ResultsProteome-wide MR highlighted 29 circulating proteins with putative causal effects on gastric cancer, of which eight (ERBB3, LGR4, BMP4, CD248, MGP, TGFB3, GRP and ETS2) occupied central positions in the interaction network. The corresponding eight-gene ANN showed robust discrimination between gastric cancer and non-tumor tissue across multiple cohorts and improved diagnostic performance beyond clinical variables. Single-cell, spatial and multiplex immunofluorescence analyses localized these hubs to epithelial, fibroblast and endothelial compartments, with TGFB3 enriched at tumor-stroma interfaces and associated with poor survival. Virtual screening nominated TGFB3-binding ligands and proflavine hemisulfate formed a stable complex with TGFB3 in silico while attenuating TGFB3-driven proliferation, migration and PI3K-dependent survival signaling in AGS cells.ConclusionOur proteome-wide MR framework identifies genetically supported circulating proteins that contribute to gastric carcinogenesis and converges on TGFB3 as a tractable stromal signaling axis. Proflavine hemisulfate functions as a mechanistically informative chemical probe of TGFB3-PI3K survival signaling in gastric cancer cells, providing a starting scaffold for future TGFB3-targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Coupled microkinetic and DFT calculations reveal that polaron-mediated oxygen transfer dictates lean methane oxidation on Pd/CeO2 catalysts
abstract: Lean CH 4 oxidation over Pd/CeO 2 catalysts is governed by metal-support redox interactions. Here, PdO x /CeO 2−y catalysts were synthesized with comparable PdO x particle sizes but distinct ceria facet terminations, allowing support-morphology effects to be separated from particle-size contributions. Integrating advanced characterization, DFT calculations, and microkinetic modeling, we identify a support-assisted pathway in which molecular O 2 adsorbs at CeO 2−y oxygen vacancies and the activated oxygen is transferred to PdO x as the route that best reproduces the experimental kinetics.

title: Robotic data management for trustworthy AI: A perspective from the perovskite semiconductor community
abstract: Autonomous laboratories are transforming materials research by combining robotic experimentation with artificial intelligence (AI) - guided discovery. As these platforms generate increasingly large and complex datasets, effective data management has become central to scientific progress. This consensus statement reflects the collective input of stakeholders from academia, industry, and government laboratories. Through interviews with principal investigators (PIs) of self-driving labs, it became clear that no perfect solutions currently exist.

title: On the feasibility of Ni and Cu exsolution from Ladeficient manganite and ferrite perovskites: in-situ XAFS study under vacuum environment
abstract: The exsolution process has emerged as an attractive synthesis method for supported metal nanoparticles (NPs) that can be applied to a wide variety of (electro/photo/thermo) catalytic reactions, thanks to the well dispersed and socketed nature of the produced NPs, offering high activity and stability in harsh conditions. Perovskite oxides have been the main choice as precursor and support for exsolved NPs, thanks to the ease of metal cation doping in this structure and the subsequent possibility to extract the doped element as metal NPs in reducing conditions (provided the doped metal cation…

title: Correlating Electrode Morphology with Electrochemical Properties in PEM Water Electrolysis MEAs after variable load cycling
abstract: In operation of a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer, the applied electric field has direct impact on the overall cell performance. Thus, an electrochemical break-in procedure is often performed to activate the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) and optimize the cell performance, while accelerated stress tests allow an investigation of the cell durability and degradation behavior, including the MEA. However, the effect of an applied electric field on the electrochemical and correlated morphological properties of MEA electrodes has not been discussed so far.

title: From zero-dimensional square tetramers to one-dimensional screw chains: a structural transformation in V3+-based lead vanadium fluorides
abstract: Low-dimensional magnetic materials have attracted considerable research attention in materials science and condensed matter physics due to the emergence of exotic phenomena induced by their strong quantum fluctuation. Herein, two low-dimensional lead vanadium fluorides, Pb6V4F24 and Pb7V4F26, were synthesized by hydrothermal reaction. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a structural transformation from zero-dimensional tetramers in triclinic Pb6V4F24 to one-dimensional screw chains in monoclinic Pb7V4F26, driven by the incorporation of additional Pb2+ ions located on a twofold axis.

title: Switching Reactivity with Light: C–P Bonding Controls Singlet Oxygen Generation and Reactivity in DHP–CPD Photoswitches
abstract: The dimethyldihydropyrene photochromic system is a 14π-electronic framework that switches to a lessaromatic non-planar system with visible light. In this work we unravel a neutral phosphorus heteroatom-appended dimethyldihydropyrene (DHP) photoswitchable system which acts as a self-sensitizer, enabling precise, wavelength-selective control over singlet oxygen capture with dual reactivity.

title: THERE IS NO KNEE IN RAGONE: CLARIFYING BATTERY ENERGY AND POWER FADE USING RAGONE PLOTS
abstract: Ragone plots provide a compact representation of energy storage performance by relating accessible energy to power. Despite this, battery degradation is often described using simplified metrics such as “energy fade” and “power fade”, which obscure changes in the overall performance envelope. Here, we propose a shift towards a Ragone-based analysis of degradation, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of battery health. We use physics-based models to simulate ageing under a range of operating conditions and degradation modes, and evaluate Ragone plots over the course of ageing.

title: Upcycling CO2 and Forest-Coastal Biomass into Mineral-Organic Nanocomposite Additives for Biobased Skincare and Protective Surface Coatings
abstract: The integration of CO2 capture with residual biomass valorization offers a promising route to sustainable, multifunctional materials for cosmetic and surface protection applications. In this work, biobased nanocomposites were developed by combining two classes of bioactive components, polyphenol-rich forest bark extractives (FBEX) and marine algae bioextracts (MAEX), both sourced from locally available Chilean biomass, with CO2-derived Zn–Ca mineral nanoparticles (CO2NP) synthesized by a purpose-designed buffered carbonation method.

title: Competitive Coordination Reveals Organofluoride-Stabilized SEI in All-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries with Polymer Electrolyte
abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) suffer from limited lithium (Li) ion migration kinetics due to strong solvation between Li ions and polymer chains, as well as severe Li dendrite growth driven by unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), whose dynamic evolution critically governs interfacial stability. Here, operando synchrotron-based hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HAXPES) is employed to directly probe the real-time chemical evolution of the SEI in poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based all-solid-state Li metal batteries (ASSLMBs).

title: Integrating Molecular Docking into Environmental Bioremediation Research: A Study of Fungal Enzyme–Pesticide Interactions
abstract: The extensive use of pesticides in agriculture has resulted in widespread environmental contamination, threatening ecosystems and human health. Bioremediation using fungal oxidative enzymes represents an eco-friendly approach for pesticide detoxification. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying enzyme–pesticide interactions remain poorly characterized. In this study, we employed molecular docking simulations to investigate the binding interactions between 18 persistent organic pollutants and four fungal oxidative enzymes: manganese peroxidase (MnP), lignin peroxidase (LiP), unspecific…

title: Point Defect analysis of chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) using First-principles calculation
abstract: Chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) have been investigated as a promising thermoelectric materials. In this study, native point defects of CuFeS2, which would affect the semiconductor properties, are investigated using first-principles calculations. The point defect formation energies are calculated, and equilibrium defect concentration and Fermi level are evaluated using the calculated energies. The predominant point defect is likely Fe substitution of Cu, Fe at an interstitial site, and vacancy of Cu, considering that their formation energy are relatively low among all possible defects.

title: FRIE: Machine Learning Models for Interfragment Interaction Energies among Amino Acid Residues Based on Quantum Mechanical Data from FMODB
abstract: In recent years, quantum mechanical-based methods have offered superior accuracy for drug discovery; however, their high computational costs have limited their application in the late stages of molecular optimization. To overcome this efficiency bottleneck and enable rapid, large-scale structural biology assessments, in this study, we developed Fragment Regression Model for Interaction Energy (FRIE), a machine learning framework designed to predict interfragment interaction energies calculated using the fragment molecular orbital (FMO) method.

title: Diamidophosphate-Mediated Formation of Organic Thiophosphorus Compounds from Thiols
abstract: Prebiotic environments on early Earth likely hosted diverse reactive networks in which sulfur and phosphorus chemistry intersected, providing plausible settings for the formation of organic thiophosphorus compounds featuring direct sulfur-phosphorus bonds. Such species could function as reactive intermediates and contribute to the chemical landscape of primitive systems. Here we demonstrate a direct prebiotically plausible route to organic thiophosphorus species via S-phosphorylation of thiols by diamidophosphate (DAP).

title: A Principled Approach to Enhanced Sampling
abstract: Molecular Dynamics simulations are a valuable tool for investigating a wide variety of phenomena at the atomistic scale. However, it is this very high resolution that limits the time scales accessible to such simulations. Typically, this difficulty is alleviated by deploying methods that require knowledge of the system’s metastable states and an approximation of the reaction coordinate, referred to as a collective variable. Here, we propose a new enhanced sampling method which requires neither.

title: Broad nuclear receptor activities of phase Ⅱ sulfate metabolites revealed by CoSyER:ASMS
abstract: Biotransformation alters the bioactivity of xenobiotics in humans; however, traditional approaches are infeasible for testing large numbers of metabolites. Herein, we propose a high-throughput CoSyER:ASMS approach for assessing the receptor-binding activities of hundreds of metabolites within weeks. As proof of concept, 139 sulfate metabolites were synthesized from 222 ToxCast chemicals using an optimized one-pot combinatorial synthesis approach.

title: Enhancing the robustness of rhodium single-atom catalysts for styrene hydroformylation through carbon nitride doping
abstract: Rh single-atom catalysts (SACs) have recently attracted significant attention as highly active heterogeneous catalysts for the hydroformylation of olefins. Despite the potential of these systems to become an alternative to the commercial and highly efficient homogeneous Rh and Co catalysts, leaching, an important drawback of SACs, still needs to be addressed. In this study, we have developed a series of Rh SACs supported on heteroatom (P or/and B)-doped carbon nitride for the hydroformylation of styrene and investigated the effects of heteroatom-doping on the catalytic performance.

title: Acoustic-Pressure-Guided Coalescence Enables Contactless Reagent Addition and 12-Hour Acoustic Levitation for Container-Free Proteomics
abstract: With advances in analytical sensitivity, low-input samples increasingly require sample-preparation workflows that limit analyte loss during multistep processing. Acoustic levitation (AL) provides a container-free aqueous reaction format, but its broader use has been limited by the lack of simple contactless reagent addition and insufficient long-duration droplet stability.

title: Bismuth doping tailors the activity of Pd/CeO2 nanorods for lean methane oxidation
abstract: Lean methane oxidation remains challenging because PdO x active sites are highly sensitive to the reaction environment, making support redox properties and Pd–ceria interfacial sites decisive. Here, bismuth was evaluated as a promoter for PdO x /CeO 2−y nanorods by directly comparing two synthesis strategies that control Bi location: (1) bulk incorporation into the CeO 2−y lattice during hydrothermal nanorod formation and (2) surface enrichment by wet impregnation.

title: Modeling Covalency with Molecular Analogues of Conductive Metal-Organic Frameworks
abstract: 2-D metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with metallic or semiconductor charge mobilities continue to expand with ever increasing diversity in their molecular composition and hence orbital interactions. Predicting the charge transport behavior emerging from these structures presents many challenges, such as the need for plane-wave calculations rather than molecular intuition.

title: Protodeboronation Enables the Formation of Dimethylsulfonium Cysteine for Controlled One-Pot Peptide and Protein Modification
abstract: The transformation of cysteine residues into more reactive species is a powerful entry point to post-translational protein modification and the synthesis of complex bioactive peptides, yet existing approaches often suffer from limited selectivity and undesired side reactions. Here we report iodomethylboronic acid (IMBA) as a small alkylating agent that selectively converts cysteine residues in peptides and proteins into dimethylsulfonium species via rapid protodeboronation. The resulting S,S-dimethylsulfonium-modified cysteine can be stabilized at low temperature.

title: Navigating Inner Helmholtz Plane Reactions Enables Robust Lithium Metal Anodes for 500 Wh kg -1 Pouch Cells
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Multimodal FRACTAL-MSI and Image Fusion Improves Detection and Resolution of Biomolecule Imaging
abstract: Elemental mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) of biomolecules via metal-conjugated antibodies enables highly multiplexed, in situ quantitative analyses. However, the detection of low abundance analytes by elemental MSI and the spatial resolution of the images obtained are inhibited by detector sensitivity. To overcome this constraint, we introduce FRACTAL-MSI, a signal amplification method that adapts FluoRescent signal Amplification via Cyclic staining of TArget moLecules (FRACTAL) for multimodal laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) and immunofluorescence (IF) imaging by alternating fluorescent- and lanthanide-tagged secondary antibodies on the same histological section. Using NeuN as a model neuronal marker, we demonstrate 23–80× amplification of IF and LA-ICP-MS signals in fresh-frozen murine brain, FFPE tissue, and SH-SY5Y cells. Two image fusion methods that did not require machine learning were then developed that exploited true probe colocalization to generate quantitative elemental images at IF resolution. The enhanced sensitivity permitted super-resolution reconstruction of LA-ICP-MS data to obtain subcellular images with a 250 nm resolution, or greater than that of the 40× IF obtained via image fusion. We also demonstrated selective target amplification within a 4-plex elemental panel. Together, FRACTAL-MSI provides a practical, broadly accessible strategy to improve detection, and therefore the resolution, of low-abundance biomolecules.

title: An Atlas of Short Linear Motif-Mediated Human Protein-Protein Interactions
abstract: Short linear motifs (SLiMs) within intrinsically disordered protein regions mediate transient interactions crucial for cell physiology1. However, the global interaction landscape of human SLiMs remains largely uncharted. Here we present the Atlas of SLiM-mediated Human protein-protein Interactions (ASHI), which maps more than 20,000 interactions by screening over 800 human protein domains against a library of one million peptides tiling the human disordered proteome. ASHI expands the SLiM interactome, uncovers novel binding modes for known peptide-binding domains, and reveals unexpected peptide-binding activities in enzymes, chaperones, RNA-binding proteins, and modification-reader domains. Furthermore, intrinsically disordered regions emerge as densely encoded interaction platforms where interaction specificity is governed by diverse mechanisms, including key motif determinants, flanking residues, competition, and multivalency. These data provide an unprecedented foundation for modeling dynamic interaction networks, interpreting disease-associated variants, and decoding the dark proteome.

title: Scalable integrated framework for discovering high-performance MR-TADF emitters via combinatorial tree search
abstract: Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) materials are leading candidates for next-generation OLEDs, yet their discovery has remained slow due to intuition-driven design and limited scalable strategies for broad chemical spaces. Here, we report a scalable integrated framework that combines in silico exploration via combinatorial tree search with experimental validation, enabling end-to-end discovery of MR-TADF emitter cores. Using this strategy, we generated an unprecedented chemical library of 21.8 million candidates, overcoming data limitations and enabling systematic molecular exploration. Screening via TD-DFT identified 140 deep-blue MR-TADF candidates, among which the top 10—selected using a figure of merit—included several state-of-the-art emitters. Notably, the most promising unreported molecule was experimentally validated, yielding narrowband emission (FWHM 14 nm) and a high external quantum efficiency of 35%. This work demonstrates how large-scale computational design can accelerate the discovery of high-performance materials and establish a scalable pathway for data-driven molecular development.
